subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose an opt-in deferred turn-maintenance timeout that releases the session lane while relying on a core fence/checkpoint to suppress late plugin side effects?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive product and lifecycle boundary: source review can establish that the implementation is coherent, but cannot choose the long-term operator contract or shutdown ownership model on behalf of the responsible maintainers.

options.title: Approve the opt-in recovery contract
options.body: Adopt the disabled-by-default setting and fenced timeout behavior as the supported way to recover a wedged background context-engine maintenance run.

options.title: Keep the existing unbounded maintenance model
options.body: Reject the new public configuration and retain current session-level recovery until a different cancellation or plugin-contract design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in recovery contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the disabled-by-default setting and fenced timeout behavior as the supported way to recover a wedged background context-engine maintenance run.
